fix_commit_message:
avcodec/adpcm: handle ADPCM_IMA_MAGIX like other similar codecs

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: 471509958/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_ADPCM_IMA_MAGIX_DEC_fuzzer-4847227777646592

We ask for a mono sample because the implementation for mono is incomplete

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 65fd5167686e on top of intro 30fc5b1baaa0 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): The ADPCM IMA Magix decoder, added in commit 30fc5b1baaa0823f134768823ab6695211d0fe21, was implemented by copying the pattern used for other similar two-channel ADPCM IMA codecs, but did not properly handle the mono case and used avctx->block_align (rather than the sample count computed by get_nb_samples()) to bound its inner decode loop. Because get_nb_samples() also lacked a dedicated branch for AV_CODEC_ID_ADPCM_IMA_MAGIX (it fell into a generic case using header_size = 4*ch), the number of output samples the frame buffer was allocated for could diverge from the number of samples actually produced by the block_align-bounded loop, and mono input streams were processed as if two full channel statuses existed. This combination led to out-of-array accesses (buffer overflow) detected by OSS-Fuzz on the ADPCM_IMA_MAGIX decoder fuzz target. Root cause: The decoder assumed the ADPCM_IMA_MAGIX bitstream always has two channels and derived its inner loop bound from avctx->block_align directly instead of from the sample count computed consistently with the output frame's allocation (get_nb_samples). No explicit handling/rejection of mono streams was added, despite the implementation only being correct for stereo.
